subject: Temporary telemetry relay subprocessor — export protocol, evidence, and rollback plan
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Acme Security <security@acmecorp.com>, Susan Lee <susan.lee@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary telemetry relay subprocessor — export protocol, evidence, and rollback plan

Hi Susan / Acme Security team,

Quick heads-up: we will be routing a small percentage of telemetry (metrics + anonymized routing metadata; no PII) through a temporary relay partner next week while we perform kernel-level telemetry upgrades in our EU region. The relay will only handle aggregated telemetry and sampling streams used for agent health and batching heuristics.

Before we flip the switch, Acme asked for the following and I want to align on what we can provide this week:
- Subprocessor manifest for the temporary relay (roles, regions, contact)
- Evidence of onshore buffering and egress controls (APAC -> EU path is sensitive for this customer)
- Short rollback / cutover runbook in case we see anomalous token-level tracing or increased latency

Kimberly / Ben / Jordan — can you confirm:
1) Which files we can share as evidence (we should avoid any raw logs).
2) The export/evidence package timeline (I think we can bundle an egress map + manifest + a snapshot).
3) The rollback TTL and a single SLACK escalation contact for the flip.

Susan / security team — acceptable formats: we can share a CSV manifest, an APAC->EU egress map PDF, and a timeboxed audit snapshot (zipped, redacted). If you need any additional attestations (KMS/HSM residency statements), flag them and we will loop in Legal.

I’m copying Procurement to keep them in the loop. We plan a tentative cutover on Tues 18 Apr (low traffic window) but will not proceed without your ack.

Thanks,

Stephanie Nguyen
Program Manager, Platform Trust
Redwood Inference
From: Susan Lee <susan.lee@acmecorp.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Security <security@acmecorp.com>, procurement@acmecorp.com
Date: Mon, 16 Apr 2028 13:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Temporary telemetry relay subprocessor — export protocol, evidence, and rollback plan

Hi Stephanie — thanks for the heads-up. A couple clarifying asks from our side:

1) Confirm that no customer identifiers (user IDs, emails, device IDs) will be routed to the relay. We only need aggregated telemetry.
2) For the manifest, we require: partner legal name, subprocessor role, country of processing, and the contract clause reference (DPA section 4.2 or equivalent).
3) For the audit snapshot: a redacted sample (schema only + example rows) is sufficient. We do expect an egress map showing which regions the relay will communicate with and whether data is persisted beyond 24 hours.

If you can provide the manifest + egress map and a brief rollback TTL (minutes to restore previous routing) by EOD tomorrow we can escalate to our Compliance team and provide a go/no-go.

S.

--
Susan Lee
Senior Security Analyst, AcmeCorp
security@acmecorp.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Susan Lee <susan.lee@acmecorp.com>, Acme Security <security@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Apr 2028 16:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary telemetry relay subprocessor — export protocol, evidence, and rollback plan

Stephanie / Susan — attaching the package we can share immediately:
- telemetry_relay_manifest_v1.csv (partner: RelayWave Ltd; role: telemetry aggregator; processing country: IE; DPA ref: Addendum A, §2.1)
- egress_map_apac-eu.pdf (diagram + interface ports; note: relay only opens outbound to our EU collector IPs; no inbound requests accepted)
- audit_snapshot_20280416.zip (redacted schema + 1 anonymized sample file; retention TTL 6 hours; no raw identifiers)

Rollback plan (summary):
- TTL to rollback routing: 7 minutes from command to full revert to direct routing (we have a hot path and prefix cache invalidation step).
- Escalation: Ben Carter (pager: +1-555-0123, slack: @benc) as primary. Jordan will run the cutover and monitor.
- Pre-cutover checks: ensure prefetched KV cache warm-up and zero-error logs for 1 hour in canary region.

Let me know if you need more granular attestations — we can generate an HSM residency note but that requires Legal sign-off (48 hours).

-kim

Kimberly Park
Senior Manager, Platform Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Susan Lee <susan.lee@acmecorp.com>, Acme Security <security@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, procurement@acmecorp.com
Date: Tue, 17 Apr 2028 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary telemetry relay subprocessor — export protocol and rollback plan (confirmed)

Susan — thanks for the quick review and confirm.

Summary and next steps:
- Package delivered (manifest + egress map + redacted snapshot). See attachments and Drive link: https://drive.google.com/telemetry-replay-manifest
- Rollback TTL: 7 minutes (Ben primary contact).
- Cutover window: Tue 18 Apr 02:00–03:00 UTC (low traffic). We will not proceed without explicit go from Acme Compliance.
- If Compliance needs the HSM/KMS residency attestation, please let us know by EOD today so we can route to Legal.

I’ll wait for final ack from Security/Procurement. If all green, Jordan and Ben will run the canary and I’ll coordinate the post-cutover evidence snapshot.

Best,

Stephanie Nguyen
Program Manager, Platform Trust
Redwood Inference
